chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Durays, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Ali ibn al-Husayn or from Muhammad ibn Ali, that he said:

Al-Fuqada' are a people who are missed from their beds, and in the morning they are found in Mecca. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'And for each is a direction toward which he turns. So compete in good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.' And they are the companions of Al-Qa'im.

key_terms.الْفُقَدَاءُ: The Missed Ones (a specific group of the Mahdi's companions)
key_terms.وَلِكُلٍّ وِجْهَةٌ: For each is a direction (Quranic phrase indicating divine guidance and gathering)
key_terms.يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا: Allah will bring you all together (divine ability to gather anywhere)

ai.seo_question: Who are the Al-Fuqada' and what is their connection to the Mahdi?
ai.summary: In al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, the 'Al-Fuqada'' are identified as the elite vanguard of the Mahdi, distinguished by their miraculous ability to vanish from their beds and reappear in Mecca, a phenomenon underscoring divine omnipotence. This tradition links their sudden mobility to the Quranic imperative to 'race to good deeds,' interpreting their physical displacement as a spiritual readiness for the final confrontation. Their status as 'companions of the Qa'im' highlights their role as the initial force that secures Mecca before the Mahdi's formal appearance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah bin Younus narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abul Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan from Dhurays from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli that Ali bin al-Husayn or Muhammad bin Ali (as) had said:

“Al-Fuqada’ are persons, who will be missed in their beds and in the morning they will be found in Mecca. It is they, who are concerned by this Qur’anic verse, ‘Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together.’ They are al-Qa’im’s companions.”
